meta.title: Lyricar, synced lyrics for whatever Spotify is playing
meta.description: Open source iOS 26 app: line-synced lyrics for your Spotify playback on the iPhone, the Lock Screen, the Dynamic Island, widgets and CarPlay.

hero.headline: Sing along to whatever Spotify is playing.
hero.sub: Synced lyrics for whatever is playing on your Spotify, on the iPhone, the Lock Screen, the Dynamic Island, widgets and CarPlay.

install.label: Get the source
install.then: Not on the App Store. You build it with Xcode 26 and your own Spotify developer app.

why.heading: How it works
body: Lyricar asks Spotify what is playing, once per second while the app is visible, and fetches line-synced lyrics for that track from LRCLIB, a public lyrics database that needs no key. Between polls a local 10 Hz clock moves the highlight, so the current line stays in step; sync drift averages about 27 ms.
You sign in to Spotify with PKCE, so there is no client secret, no backend and no analytics. Your phone talks to Spotify and to LRCLIB, and to nothing else.
why.highlight: No secret, no backend, no analytics.

items.title: Karaoke on the iPhone
items.body: The current line lights up as it is sung. Tap any line to seek there, and nudge a track a little later or earlier if its timing is off.

items.title: Lock Screen and Dynamic Island
items.body: A Live Activity carries the current line onto the Lock Screen and into the Dynamic Island. iOS 26 also shows it on the CarPlay dashboard.

items.title: Five widgets
items.body: Lyric Line, Up Next, Remote, Verse and Gauge. Their buttons work even with the app terminated.

items.title: A CarPlay app
items.body: Karaoke, Focus, Stage and Track tabs, built for a glance at the screen in the car.

items.title: Eight styles
items.body: Midnight, Motorsport, Night Drive, Panoramic, Sport, Luxe, Neon and Daylight, applied across the app, the widgets and CarPlay.

items.title: Nothing in between
items.body: Spotify PKCE sign-in and the public LRCLIB API. No server of ours, no account, no tracking.

install.heading: Build it yourself
install.intro: You need a Mac with Xcode 26, Homebrew, and a Spotify developer app of your own.

steps.title: Generate the project
steps.body: XcodeGen writes the Xcode project; the setup script asks for your Spotify client ID and signing details.

steps.title: Open and run
steps.body: Pick your iPhone or a Simulator and press Run.

install.note: Your Spotify app stays in Development Mode: up to 5 users, and its owner needs Spotify Premium. The README has every step.
